A new international body known as the Board of Peace has been created to oversee the Gaza ceasefire and reconstruction efforts, but its formation has sparked controversy and divided reactions around the world.

This report examines why countries including France, Spain, Germany and Canada declined participation or faced disputes over membership. Critics have raised concerns that the initiative could weaken the role of the United Nations, while others question the structure of the board and Donald Trump's role as permanent chairman.

Several Arab and Muslim countries accepted invitations with conditions focused on ending the war and supporting Gaza's recovery. The report also explores why the exclusion of the UN and Palestine has become a major point of debate.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US President Donald Trump has announced what he describes as a major breakthrough in efforts to end the conflict in Gaza, saying an agreement has been reached for the phased disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups.

According to the plan, weapons would be surrendered in stages, Israeli forces would gradually withdraw, and a new Palestinian police force—supported by an international stabilization mission—would assume responsibility for security in Gaza.

The announcement follows meetings between Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Washington and comes after reports that Hamas has agreed to the framework, although official statements from the parties are still awaited.

This report examines what the proposed agreement includes, the role of regional mediators including Qatar, Egypt and Türkiye, the humanitarian implications for Gaza, and the political challenges that could determine whether the plan succeeds.
